title: An ECG and a student
stem:
You are an F2 doctor in cardiology. You are about to sign off a medical student's assessment, which needs to be submitted today.

A nurse asks you to look at an ECG for a patient with new chest pain, saying it may show an ST-elevation myocardial infarction.
instruction: Choose the 3 most appropriate actions to take in this situation.

options.text: Finish signing off the assessment first, as it will take five minutes.
options.detailed: Five minutes may seem small, but in a STEMI, delays matter.

options.text: Ask the student to look at the ECG while you finish the assessment.
options.brief: A student can't assess a possible STEMI.
options.detailed: This may be a learning opportunity later, but a qualified doctor needs to assess the ECG now.

options.text: Ask the nurse to repeat the ECG and call you back.
options.brief: Delays assessment of a possible STEMI.
options.detailed: A repeat ECG may be useful, but you need to look at the first one now.

options.text: Look at the ECG straight away.
options.brief: A possible STEMI needs immediate review.
options.detailed: If the ECG shows a STEMI, the patient needs urgent treatment, and every minute matters.

options.text: Sign off the assessment without reviewing it, to save time.
options.brief: Dishonest, and unfair to the student.
options.detailed: This would mean signing an assessment you haven't reviewed.

options.text: Get the cardiology registrar to see the patient with you.
options.brief: A possible STEMI needs senior input quickly.
options.detailed: The registrar can confirm the ECG findings and arrange urgent treatment, such as primary angioplasty.

options.text: Tell the student you can't sign the assessment today.
options.brief: Unnecessary, as you can finish it later today.
options.detailed: The patient comes first, but you can still help the student meet the deadline.

options.text: Apologise to the student and agree a time to finish the assessment today.
options.brief: Respects the student's deadline while prioritising the patient.
options.detailed: The student's assessment matters, and agreeing a time to finish it today makes sure they aren't disadvantaged.

explanation.issue: This tests whether you prioritise a potential emergency while still respecting a colleague's needs.
explanation.keyDetails: The ECG may show a STEMI. The assessment is due today but isn't urgent in clinical terms.
explanation.reasoning: [D] looks at the ECG, [F] brings senior help, and [H] respects the student's deadline. The distractors delay ([A], [C]), inappropriately delegate ([B]), or are dishonest or unnecessary ([E], [G]).
explanation.competing: [G] may seem honest, but you can finish the assessment later in the day.

references.title: Good medical practice
references.note: Domain 1, prioritising patients according to clinical need.
